claims.statement: Current detailed guide requires Workspace access and Workflow steps connections. Finish both setup cards for the intended organization and Attio workspace. Every block requires the Neon Deer connection; use managed app connections rather than putting an API key into Code inputs. Scheduling needs an organization time zone. Lookup execution and subflows require the relevant paid/trial access; verify current account entitlements.

claims.statement: Reference data belongs here when workflows need mappings that are not CRM records: geography-to-owner, status-to-SLA or member-to-Slack mention. Each lookup matches one unique key after type normalization; no fuzzy, range or compound matching. Lookup key and Return to workflows are separate settings. Shared fields alone become outputs. Custom/library tables start with fields unshared. Synced members provide editable Slack IDs and computed mentions. Status tables preserve custom metadata but exclude archived statuses from matching. Workflows read tables; no table-write workflow step is documented. Starter copies are independent, while member/status tables sync from Attio. Plan and management permission are separate from Attio roles. Export/import may alter formula-like values through protective apostrophes.
claims.scope: Published Neon Deer documentation, with source conflicts retained. No live setup or execution tested.

claims.statement: One-time per-record dispatch via bulk selection or Schedule a workflow run. Separate scheduling actions can create multiple follow-ups. Pending schedules follow the workflow, not a frozen published version. Turning off does not cancel; due runs can be skipped. Deleting a record does not cancel its schedule. Sent means the trigger endpoint accepted dispatch, not that downstream work succeeded. Inspect Attio runs for effects. Time selection uses organization time zone. Bulk dialog offers quarter hours; nonexistent DST times are rejected and repeated times choose the first occurrence. Do not generalize UI granularity to the timestamp step. Upcoming and History show schedules; the record widget shows pending runs. Cancellation is unavailable while a send is underway. Partial batch acceptance requires reconciliation before rescheduling.
claims.scope: Published Neon Deer documentation, with source conflicts retained. No live setup or execution tested.

claims.statement: Start a subflow defines object, starting-point name and named text inputs; callers pass the typed record separately. Call a subflow waits by default; detailed docs specify 15 minutes. dont_wait continues without returned fields. Return from a subflow uses this run’s subflow_id, a status and five text output slots. First return wins. Keep caller mappings synchronized after changing named inputs. Review both runs before retrying a timed-out call because previous effects may already exist.

claims.statement: Platform Activity covers reported app trigger/step events, not every block of the full Attio workflow. Needs attention groups unacknowledged failures. find-aggregate-update.body:
# Find, aggregate, and update a record

This recipe describes a graph pattern observed in a production workflow and connects it to separately tested Playground block behavior. **The combined graph was not newly validated as one end-to-end recipe.** The production projection redacts the literal filter values and aggregation choice, so use the owning workflow's current configuration and permissions when adapting it.

Capability references: Guard, Find Records, Aggregate Values, and Update Record.

## Bindings

1. Route the record-update trigger through a guard so the calculation only continues when its predicate matches.
2. Configure Find Records with the relevant object and a filter derived from the trigger context. Its `done.records` output feeds Aggregate Values' `values` input. In the observed production graph, the filter compares an entity-attribute path against a reference from the trigger.
3. Select the numeric attribute from each matched record in Aggregate Values. Set `aggregation_type` to the intended operation. The production projection does not reveal which operation it used. In the separate Playground test, valid values were `sum`, `mean`, `min`, and `max`; the UI's “Average” label maps to `mean`.
4. Map Aggregate Values' `done.total` output into the numeric or currency attribute configured on Update Record, and use the intended record reference as its target.

## Expected typed outputs

Find Records returns `done.records` and `done.match_count`. Aggregate Values returns `done.total` as a number. Update Record completes with a record reference; the observed production configuration maps the aggregate total to an attribute typed as a number/currency union. The production evidence does not establish the resulting stored value.

## Verification and limits

The production graph structure and bounded historical run statuses are recorded in the review catalog under `guarded-find-aggregate-update-union`, with supporting config and run samples in the source catalog. That catalog explicitly says the samples do not prove this exact pattern executed. The production `aggregation_type` literal is redacted.

Separate Playground evidence covers a two-record Find Records → Aggregate Values calculation (compute/time catalog) and an Update Record effect on a synthetic record (run, independent verification). These checks do not combine the blocks into a newly tested workflow. Verify filter scope, operation, target record, attribute type, and resulting public record state in an authorized test before relying on the composed behavior.

http-parse-code.body:
# Fetch, parse, and consume typed JSON

This is a tested Playground pattern: Send HTTP Request returns a JSON string, Parse JSON validates and exposes typed fields, and Execute Code consumes a parsed number.

Capability references: Send HTTP Request, Parse JSON, and Execute Code.

## Bindings

1. Configure Send HTTP Request with `method`, `url`, and `headers`. The tested GET used an empty headers array and a synthetic JSON response.
2. Map `Send HTTP Request.done.response_body` to Parse JSON's `input`. Supply a JSON Schema string requiring `count` as a number; the tested schema also allowed an optional string `tag`.
3. Add a Code input named `count`, type `number`, and map it from `Parse JSON.done.parsed.count`. In `async function main(inputs)`, return or use `inputs.count`.

## Expected typed outputs

For the successful fixture, HTTP returned `response_status` as number `200`, `response_body` as a string containing `{"count":7,"tag":"synthetic"}`, and `response_ok` as boolean `true`. Parse JSON returned `done.parsed.count` as number `7` and `done.parsed.tag` as string `synthetic`. Execute Code returned a string containing serialized JSON `{"seen":7}`.

## Verification and limits

The exact typed bindings are in the synthetic fixture (`/configs/parse`, `/configs/code`, and `/cases/valid/http_config`). The runtime runs and verification confirm the valid path and failures for missing required `count`, wrong type, and malformed JSON. A missing optional `tag` succeeded.

The related HTTP response checks show that a non-2xx HTTP response can still complete the block with `response_ok=false`; inspect status/ok before parsing. HTTP method, authentication, interpolation, timeouts, and transport failures were not covered. The Parse JSON UI editor was not captured; webhook input and broader schema cases remain unverified. Do not pass credentials as Code inputs without accounting for evaluated-config retention: the Find/Code discovery catalog records that a secret-valued variable appeared in evaluated config.

retry-with-live-workflow.body:
# Retry a failed run with the currently published workflow

Retry with live workflow uses the original run's completed trigger execution as the retry source and targets the compatible trigger block on a newer published version. In the observed synthetic case, this created a new linked run on the new version and replayed the workflow from that trigger.

Capability references: Workflow logs, Workflow lifecycle, Workflow triggers, and Execute Code.

## Parameter bindings

Use the original workflow ID, immutable source version, source run ID, root frame ID, and **completed original trigger execution ID** in the retry route. Set `target_workflow_version_id` to the newly published immutable version and `target_workflow_version_block_instance_id` to that version's matching compatible trigger block. Mint fresh UUIDs for `retry_workflow_version_run_id`, `retry_root_workflow_version_run_frame_id`, and `retry_trigger_workflow_version_run_frame_block_execution_id`.

The observed endpoint shape is `POST /workflows/{workflow}/versions/{source_version}/runs/{source_run}/frames/{root_frame}/block-executions/{original_trigger_execution}/retry`. Use a captured, verified route and request shape for the target workspace; this description is not a client-ready API helper.

## Expected output and verification

The response identifies a new linked run on the target version. Read that run, its frames, and block executions separately; verify the expected blocks completed and inspect the relevant typed outcome data. The controlled test repaired a deliberately failing Code block, published a new version with the same Manual trigger, then retried from the original completed Manual trigger. The resulting run completed on the new version with the safe success marker.

The captured UI request, synthetic run evidence, and API contract entry document the concrete request and result. A request that used the failed Code execution as the retry source/target was rejected with `TRIGGER_BLOCK_EXECUTION_INVALID`; use the original completed trigger execution and matching trigger block instead.

## Status and limits

This cross-version retry was verified on one owned synthetic Manual-trigger workflow. Attio's help article describes retries as attempts under the same run, while the observed live-workflow retry created a new run ID; treat the request shape as a bounded observed behavior. Compatibility was not tested across other trigger types. Starting again at a trigger can repeat downstream side effects, so inspect the graph and effects before initiating a retry. The test workflow was paused afterward.

neon-deer-territory-routing.body:
# Territory lookup → owner update → Slack mention

**Evidence: documented composition with a narrated video demonstration. Not
independently executed or captured as an API template.** See the
guide and
[walkthrough](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TYjbnjf22as).

## Bindings and graph

Resolve the client's workspace, company object, territory attribute, owner
attribute, app installation/connections, table IDs and Slack destination.
Create/import a territory table with a unique territory key and a **Workspace
member** owner column. Share the owner output with workflows. Populate each
member's correct Slack ID in the synced workspace-members table.

1. Native attribute-change trigger supplies the changed company and new territory.
2. Neon Deer Find lookup table row selects the territory table/key and uses the
   new territory value. Branch on `found` and an available owner.
3. Native Update Record sets the triggering company's owner to the returned
   typed member. Do not target a company ID retained in a demo capture.
4. Second Neon Deer lookup finds that member in the workspace-members table.
5. After a successful match and nonempty mention, native Slack sends the agreed
   message to the client's chosen destination using the computed mention.

Missing mappings should route to an explicit fallback/review path. A record owner
update and Slack delivery are distinct effects; failure of the second does not
undo the first. Avoid resending an alert blindly after a partial run.

## Acceptance before reuse

In an authorized test, change one synthetic company's territory. Inspect both
lookup outputs, verify the stored owner, and separately verify the intended
Slack recipient/message. Also try an unmapped territory and missing Slack ID.
The source demo assigns all Slack mappings to one test user; that is not a
portable client mapping. No message was sent by this research pass.

update record,
Slack.

# Reuse a subflow with a text identity input

**Evidence: documentation and a narrated walkthrough, supplemented by Playground captures, email member lookup cases and successful literal/dynamic caller-child roundtrips. This
member-email lookup composition has not been executed.** The guide
explains setup and provider limits. Source:
[subflow video at 05:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lwD3I-8LLfA&t=345).

## Order of setup (verified 2026-10-22)

1. Connect the app to a Neon Deer org.
2. Build the subflow, then publish it **and turn it Live**.
3. Only then pick it in each caller's Call block, in the UI.

The picker lists only active subflows. Without the org connection, the Call
panel errors ("This block is no longer supported"). The full checklist is in the
guide, and
the evidence is in the
picker probe.

## Bindings and graph

Choose the client's object, active subflow entry point, typed record, named input
key and member identity source. Do not mix IDs from different workspaces.

1. Start a subflow defines the object and a named text input such as `member_email`.
2. Caller selects the same object, destination and typed record, and maps an
   email string to that input. Missing named inputs arrive as empty text.
3. Subflow uses Find workspace member with the email input; branch on its count.
   Convert value does not produce a typed workspace member. If a later step
   needs that type, use the member returned by the find step.
4. Return from a subflow maps **this execution's** Subflow ID, status and intended
   text result slots. Return on each intended completion path; first return wins.
5. Waiting caller inspects returned status before using text output. With
   installed `wait_for_result=false` (legacy `dont_wait` is a separate schema field), it receives `started` and cannot consume return fields.

The installed Playground caller offers 1, 3, 5, 10 and 15-minute timeouts
(`timeout_minutes`, string enum), plus `wait_for_result`. Start saves named
`output_definitions`; Return saves an `outputs` array whose order follows Start.
These captures supersede the older fixed-timeout/five-slot configuration description
for this bundle. Waited literal and two-field dynamic input-to-return roundtrips are runtime verified. Return resolves the current Subflow ID; a failed Return still selects `returned`, with status `Failed`, so check that status. Non-waiting Call with `wait_for_result=false` completed before its correlated child and returned no awaited output. Call
uses a UI-selected three-part JSON-array string (workflow, trigger, opaque token).
See current roundtrip evidence. Re-check caller mappings after
renaming inputs. See the live evidence.

## Acceptance before reuse

Test one matching email, one absent identity, and the empty-input path in an
owned fixture. Inspect both caller and child logs, mapped values and final
outputs. A one-minute configured no-Return case failed after its harmless child completed (about 112 seconds overall). A timeout does not undo child effects; inspect before rerunning. This
recipe does not implement arbitrary typed arguments, typed return slots, or an
API adapter for creating app blocks.

Capabilities: start,
call,
member lookup,
return.

guides.workflows:
# Author and inspect workflows

Start with the capability index and resolve the intended workspace through
client bindings. This guide concerns modern workflows.
Public record/task/note operations and internal workflow authoring are separate
capabilities. The reusable builder now supports new owned
Manual → Find Records → Code → Update Record workflows with explicit bindings,
configuration edits and lifecycle operations. Read its bounded supported format
before selecting a runner. The repository's experimental workflow clients are pinned to
Playground or explicit read-only review assignments; they are not generic client
runners.

## Select the operation

- Lifecycle: draft/config/path,
  commit/activate, manual trigger, observed retry modes, deactivate/archive.
- Trigger inventory: standard
  forms with per-trigger evidence; Manual and Record action have runtime proof.
- Block references: actual provider versions, typed inputs,
  output names and the limits of each block's evidence.
- Run inspection: historical runs,
  frames, attempts, evaluated inputs and outputs.
- Production review:
  read-only assignments and reusable pattern occurrences.

## Build a connected draft

1. Read fresh workspace, workflow and draft identities. Read the graph before
   changing it. Resolve block provider slug/version from its capability entry.
2. Write a typed configuration node under `config`; the server's read response
   may wrap that node in `config.state` and `config.value`. Do not send that whole
   read wrapper as the typed config.
3. Connect paths using source/target block IDs and the observed source outcome.
   Find/Code/Aggregate commonly use `done`; Loop's item path uses `next`. Copy
   each block's actual protocol rather than assuming a universal outcome.
4. Read the complete graph/config back and compare with the intended change.
   Missing paths and invalid provider versions can survive a successful save.
   `config.state=complete` alone does not establish required-field validity.
5. Follow the task's existing authorization for publication/run. Commit creates
   an immutable version; activation enables execution. Capture the resulting
   version ID rather than continuing to inspect the mutable draft.

Exact routes and request shapes are indexed in the
observed contract. It is dated
protocol evidence, not a universal write permit. Discovery registries and exact
config grants apply to their original owned Playground fixtures only.

## Inspect a run or diagnose a failure

Keep `(workflow, immutable version, run, frame, block execution, attempt)` together.
Read run metadata, frames, then block executions. The execution collection is a
list, not an object keyed by block. Preserve repeated attempts rather than
assuming one execution per block in every workflow.

Inspect block status/outcome and `error_message`, `failure_reason`, or older
`error`. Read evaluated inputs and outcome data separately when their availability
flags permit it. Returned outputs are typed under `runtime_value`; their field
names belong to the block's capability reference. A workflow status of completed
is not proof of every intended external effect; verify the specific effect where
possible.

Evaluated Code inputs have exposed a supplied credential in a tested run. Avoid
saving sensitive inputs, prompts, raw HARs or broad production records into the
catalog. Preserve exact discriminator values and synthetic literals when they
are safe—shape-only data that turns every `type` into `string` is not a request
example.

## Retry and finish

The tested live-workflow retry starts from the original trigger execution and
points to the same compatible trigger on the newly published version. It created
a linked new run in the observed case. Retry from failed has different semantics.
Use the retry recipe, not a guessed
source execution. Reconcile an uncertain request/run ID before submitting again.

Deactivation prevents new runs; it does not cancel existing ones. Archive with
`is_archived=true` after confirming inactivity. Verify both `is_archived=true`
and `active_workflow_version_id=null`; the status may remain paused or draft.
Workflow deletion is outside this toolset's tested lifecycle. Restore, in-flight
control and successful-run rerun are not established by these archive tests.

## Neon Deer extension patterns

For shared subflows, reference-data lookup, per-record future runs, set comparisons
and extra task/note events, consult the Neon Deer app guide
before adding custom code. Its catalog is documentation-backed; no new app-provider
authoring adapter was added to the bounded workflow builder.
guides.workflow-blocks:
# Choose a workflow block reference

Search the capability index for the block label or
provider slug, or use the local catalog search described in the toolkit README.
Each `workflow.block.*` entry gives the observed provider version, input/output
keys, exact configuration evidence, bounded claims and remaining gaps.

Read the full configuration example and its claim scope before composing a new
block. Examples may contain fixture IDs and synthetic literals; replace target
bindings and upstream references. Entries are protocol references, not executable
client-specific templates. The repository's dated experiment scripts may mutate
immediately and must not be run simply because a reference links to them.

## Build from current evidence

1. Prefer the public API for ordinary record, list, task or note operations when
   supported. Workflow graph/config authoring is the internal-API capability.
2. Use the captured provider slug and version. Version acceptance on a save does
   not guarantee a supported editor or runnable block.
3. Use actual config keys and typed values, then connect the graph. Follow
   variables and the correct filter grammar.
4. Distinguish a saved configuration from an executed case and a verified effect.
   Read the entry's gaps before generalizing its example.

Examples of details that matter: Aggregate Average is `mean`, Minimum is `min`,
Maximum is `max`; `average` saved but failed runtime schema validation. Slack is
an app-provider block. A Slack config reported `complete` while its required
Channel was absent. Neither saving that config nor reading an existing client
workflow proves message delivery.

The custom-agent reference
also routes to a retained run with three Attio read-tool calls. The
Loop reference includes a
two-record Find-to-Loop-to-Code case. These narrow extensions correct older
blanket gaps without establishing every tool group or array behavior.

## Neon Deer app extensions

Use the Neon Deer app guide before implementing custom
Code or a large Switch tree for reference lookups, record scheduling, subflows
or set comparisons. The `workflow.app.neondeer.*` catalog entries cover the
published inventory and video patterns. They are documentation references, not
captured provider configs; do not transfer native block schemas to similarly
named app blocks. App Find tasks also has its own flat filtering contract.

## Research boundaries

The curated block entries cover the investigated record/list actions, conditions,
Loop, HTTP/Parse JSON, Find/Code, Custom Agent, tasks/notes, computation/time and
messaging. Standard triggers are routed through their own capability inventory.
Other AI blocks, sequences and Enterprise SQL were not selected for this pass.
The historical provider inventory is broader than the verified capability set.

Consult research provenance if two older files
conflict or an example needs deeper investigation. Keep the failure evidence;
promote only the exact behavior that later evidence resolves.
guides.variables:
# Map workflow variables

The variable capability
collects exact examples and their verification limits. A variable refers to an
upstream block's outcome and traverses its output with ordered operations.

A matcher identifies the upstream block, outcome, and operations such as a
`field` followed by an `attribute-definition`. An optional `as` describes the
cast. These are typed protocol nodes; preserve their discriminator values.
Generate matcher IDs for the new graph and resolve object/attribute IDs from the
target workspace. Do not copy historical graph or attribute IDs across clients.

## Select the actual output

Consult the source block's capability entry before mapping
an input. For example, Formula emits `done.result`; Aggregate emits `done.total`;
Adjust time emits `done.adjusted_timestamp`. Those names are not interchangeable.
Output API responses wrap typed values in `runtime_value`; a saved matcher uses
operations over the block outcome, not a literal HTTP response JSON pointer.

Find Records to Aggregate demonstrates
`records` followed by an attribute-definition operation, producing a numeric
array. Execute Code inputs require their observed name/value/type wrapper; use
its full configuration example rather than pasting a bare matcher as the whole
block config.

For a Loop record item, casting the item directly to string produced its display
name in the tested case. Traverse the record's `record_id` attribute before
casting when the consumer requires an ID.

## Handle editor and runtime limits

Connect a compatible upstream path before expecting variable choices in the
editor. An unconnected task step showed “No accessible blocks.” A literal typed
task/record reference has separate execution evidence; that does not prove every
task-variable conversion.

Multiple matchers and a numeric fallback were saved and read back, but their
runtime precedence was not tested. Rich-text variable spans have their own
serialization; use block-specific evidence. Slack interpolation remains a gap.
Do not infer it from another app's message payload.

Passing an API key through a variable does not make it a secret store: the tested
Code evaluated-input log contained that value. Client mappings must reference
credential sources without embedding their values in examples or catalogs.

## Neon Deer app inputs

Neon Deer subflows
pass a typed record separately from named text inputs and text returns. Resolve
member emails with Find workspace member when a typed member is needed; Convert
value still returns text. These app input keys do not establish serialized
variable matcher shapes.
guides.filters:
# Choose the correct filter grammar

First identify the surface, then resolve attribute type and subfield. Similar
labels in Attio do not imply interchangeable request formats. Start with the
following references rather than searching every dated investigation.

| Surface | Current reference | Key distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Find Records | Capability | `entity-filter` trees; presence uses `unary-filter.left` |
| Find Tasks | Block reference | Task-specific object/attribute IDs; exact Created at case verified |
| Find List Entries | Block reference | Resolve the list and its attributes; do not substitute object filters blindly |
| Filter and If | Conditions | Typed predicates; presence uses `unary-predicate.operand` |
| Saved views | View filters | Persisted filter blocks and identities, separate from workflow expressions |
| Reports | Report filters and report guide | Saved filter blocks differ from dataset `and`/`or` query trees; preserve saved dynamic tokens and resolve list versus linked-record paths |

## Construct and verify a workflow Find filter

Resolve the target attribute's type, ID, object/list identity, path and subfield.
Then use the operator matrix
for the matching attribute type. A captured dropdown is UI evidence; only cases
with execution evidence establish tested matching behavior.

For the sampled date attributes, before/after use `less-than`/`greater-than`;
timestamps use `before`/`after`. A sampled date `is not` comparison also matched
missing values. Add an explicit not-empty condition when the intended semantics
require a value. Do not apply these observations to every multi-value type.

Nested AND/OR Find groups use `composite-filter` with `operator` and `operands`.
The structural constructors prevent mixing
Find expressions with predicates; they do not validate live attribute compatibility.
Test expected matching and nonmatching records after constructing the expression.

## Resolve older conflicting examples

The later relative-date evidence
clarifies that the tested date comparison with `-P6M` means six months ago;
`P6M` means six months in the future. It also establishes a variable date RHS.
The older probe's contrary direction assumption must not be reused.

For the tested relationship-presence case, `target_entity_instance_id` worked
in the editor and runtime. `target_record_id` ran but appeared unknown in the
editor. This presence test does not establish arbitrary relationship traversal;
other multi-hop cases remain unresolved.

Use exact examples from the capability entry, replace fixture IDs with current
bindings, and preserve their typed literals/operators. Validate both saved
configuration and actual matches. HTTP success alone is insufficient.

## Neon Deer app finds

The Neon Deer app has separate Find tasks and Find notes
steps with flat documented options, plus typed equality lookup tables. Do not
apply native Find Records or Guard predicate grammar to these provider contracts.
Read `workflow.app.neondeer.step.find-tasks` or the corresponding app entry first.
guides.neon-deer-automations:
# Neon Deer Advanced Workflow Automations

**Installation prerequisite:** These capabilities come from the **Neon Deer Advanced Workflow Automations app** and require that app to be installed and connected in the target Attio workspace. Complete both **Workspace access** and **Workflow steps** connections, then verify block availability, permissions and feature entitlement for that client. An Attio API key alone does not provide these blocks. If the app is absent, identify installation/setup as a dependency before building a workflow that uses them.

All app block entries use `workflow.app.neondeer.*` IDs and “Neon Deer” titles. Observed installed providers have `type=app` with the app ID; native Attio blocks use system providers. Check provider identity even when labels overlap. The documented Check primary value block remains unavailable in the inspected installation; installing the app does not establish that every documented block is present.

Use this app when a workflow needs reusable subflows, reference-data lookups,
per-record future runs, precise multi-value differences, additional task/note
triggers, or meeting/comment data. It combines **Attio workflow blocks** with the
**Neon Deer platform**, which manages lookup tables, connections, scheduled runs
and app activity. It was previously called Workflow Utilities.

This reference is based on 42 public documentation articles and seven walkthrough
transcripts reviewed October 22, 2026. There are **34 blocks in the written
inventory (12 triggers, 22 steps)**, plus **two additional scheduling candidates
from the video**. A subsequent Playground live pass captured installed providers/configuration and executed selected blocks.
A second Playground pass adds the remaining forms, typed comparison runs, synthetic event triggers and further data/lifecycle tests. The installed Record deleted trigger increases the catalog to 37 block entries, including documented Check primary value, which remains absent from the picker.
The third Playground pass reconciles **36 installed blocks plus one documented absent block**. Across passes, 34 have bounded functional runtime evidence; the transcript getter has invalid-input-only evidence, the recording trigger configuration only, and Check primary value is absent.
The written inventory is not an exhaustive installed-provider inventory, and
coverage is explicitly separated into documentation, UI, config and runtime evidence.

Start with the app capability,
then search `workflow.app.neondeer.*` in the catalog.
Each block entry links to its exact documented fields and limitations in the
dated catalog.

## Choose a simpler composition

| Need | Use | What it avoids / what to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Territory → owner, status → SLA, member → Slack recipient | Find lookup table row | Replaces a growing Switch tree or mapping embedded in Code. Set typed lookup keys and shared output fields. |
| Shared logic called from several workflows | Start a subflow → Call a subflow → Return from a subflow | Centralizes logic. Record is typed; named inputs and returned slots are text. |
| Follow up for one record at a future time | Start a scheduled run + bulk action or Schedule a workflow run | Separates one-time record scheduling from recurring scans and a long-running Delay. |
| Identify exactly which linked records/users/values changed | Compare records / members / values | Avoids looping every current value or writing set-difference code. Previous = A, new = B. |
| Notify a record owner in Slack | Member lookup table → native Slack step | One shared mapping replaces separate owner-specific message branches. |
| React to task status, assignee, deadline or deletion | App task triggers | Requires tracked prior task state; first unknown event may only initialize state. |
| Process a call recording | Call recording created → Get call transcript | Handle `not_ready` and incomplete results explicitly. |
| Normalize an input | Convert value | Validates/formats text; it does **not** produce a typed member, record or numeric token. |

## Setup and provider identity

The current setup guide and installation transcript require **both Workspace
access and Workflow steps connections** for the intended organization/workspace.
All app blocks need the Neon Deer connection. Use the app's managed connections;
these patterns do not require copying an API key into a Code block. Scheduling
also needs the organization's time zone. Verify current plan/trial entitlements
for lookup execution, scheduling and subflows; this library does not fix prices
or subscription limits.

The platform's table-management permissions are separate from Attio membership.
A configured workspace connection does not establish that a particular user can
manage tables. Multiple installed copies, including development apps, can expose
similar labels. **Create note, Find tasks, Task created and Call recording created
must be distinguished by provider**, not merely by their display name.

The live pass identified the production app provider (`app_id`
`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000018`) and selected `app_block_id` values.
Its provider has no explicit version field; install/bundle IDs identify the captured
schema context. Exact draft wrappers and selected run results are in the dated
live catalog. Named subflow inputs and dynamic return mappings are verified; arbitrary cross-block compositions remain untested. The
existing workflow builder supports its bounded
Manual → Find Records → Code → Update Record path; adding these catalog entries
does not add general app-block execution support. Task-local probes are separately
classified in the tool inventory. Documentation URL slugs are not provider IDs.

The existing Playground app connection successfully served lookup and selected
utility/data blocks without signing into the separate platform. This does not
prove permission to manage tables or entitlement for every app feature. Several
configuration panels call read-only app server functions; blocking those in a
recorder causes Loading/errors, which must not be reported as app failures.
A saved `config.state=complete` also appears on incomplete forms: validate
required fields, graph paths and exact intended effects before publishing.

## Lookup tables: model the mapping once

Tables can start blank, from CSV/library data, or from synced workspace members
and status values. Geography/industry/free-domain tables supply starter data;
copies are independent. Synced member and status tables track Attio identities
while retaining custom metadata such as Slack ID, owner or SLA.

Select a table and lookup definition, then supply the value in the field's type.
A lookup uses one unique typed key; it is not a fuzzy/range/compound query. In a
territory table, import the owner as **Workspace member**, not Text. A string ID
in an untyped column does not establish a usable member output.

**Lookup key** controls how a row is found. **Return to workflows** controls
which fields appear as outputs. Custom/library fields start unshared. Branch on
`found`; absent values can be omitted, while zero, false and empty text are
retained. Shared field types become locked in the documented circumstances.
Changing/removing the selected key requires caller review; there is no fallback.

For Slack, populate the correct Slack member ID in each synced member row and
use its computed mention (`<@ID>`) in the Slack message block. The video maps every
demo row to one test recipient; do not copy that business mapping into a client.
No table-write workflow block is documented. Treat missing/archived statuses and
incomplete mappings as deliberate branches, rather than silently assigning an
arbitrary owner.

## Subflows: typed record, text boundary

### Setting up a subflow (checklist)

Evidence: picker probe 2026-10-22 (Playground + i-5).

1. **Connect the app to a Neon Deer organization first.** In the workspace, go to
   Settings → Apps → Advanced Workflow Automations. Without that connection:
   - the subflow's activation fails (its Start block needs the org);
   - the Call panel shows "This block is no longer supported / Something went
     wrong while loading this block", because its list returns
     `no-workspace-connection`.
2. **Build the subflow:**
   - Start a subflow: the object, then named inputs/outputs.
   - The steps.
   - Return from a subflow: this run's `subflow_id`, a status, and the outputs
     in Start's order.
3. **Publish it AND turn it Live.** The Call picker lists only **active**
   subflows:
   - draft-only or committed-but-inactive subflows are missing;
   - a paused subflow drops out within seconds.
4. **Then configure each caller's Call block.**
   - Pick the object, then the subflow **in the UI**. The saved `workflow_id` is
     `["<callee>", "<Start block id>", "<opaque token>"]`. Never hand-build it.
     Copying the exact value from another caller in the *same* workspace gives
     the same bytes (verified), but the token differs between workspaces.
   - After picking, check:
     - **Record**: no warning in the field;
     - **Wait for a result**;
     - **Timeout** (1/3/5/10/15 min);
     - one field per named input (blank = empty text);
     - the panel shows no "This input is required".
5. **Cut over:** test one record through the new caller, then switch off the old
   path before turning the new caller Live. Never run both at once.

Gotchas:
- The picker shows the **active** version's input names. Unpublished draft edits
  don't appear until republished.
- Republishing keeps the same Start block id. An existing pick keeps working
  **only if the inputs and outputs are unchanged** (verified). Re-check named-input
  mappings if you renamed inputs.
- **Changing the Start outputs and republishing breaks every existing pick** (i-5,
  2026-10-22). Each Call panel then shows "Invalid option value: […]" and "Choose
  the subflow again to load its current outputs". Re-picking gives a new token, with
  the same workflow and Start ids. So the token follows the output definitions:
  re-pick in every caller after an output change.
- The picker lists only subflows on the Call block's object. A People subflow
  doesn't appear for a Companies Call.
- **A list mapped into a Return output arrives as its first item only.** For
  example, a Parse JSON array `written` returned just its first element. Return a
  JSON string instead.
- **Never end a subflow path with a Filter (guard) that can stop the run.** No
  Return means the waiting caller fails at its timeout, which also stops a caller's
  loop. Use an If (`system/branch`) with a Return on both branches.
- A Call **Record** fed by Find records (limit 1, "Matched Companies") shows an amber
  "first value" notice but passes the right record at runtime (i-5 test, 2026-10-22).
- Credit overhead per call: Call 1 + Return 1 (Start, If, Parse JSON 0). Measured
  on i-5 with a Custom agent subflow: 12 credits against 10 inline.
- Pausing a subflow breaks every caller at runtime: "That subflow is turned off.
  Turn it on in Attio, then choose it again."

### Block details

1. Define the object and distinct named text inputs/outputs in Start a subflow.
   The installed form saves `input_definitions` and `output_definitions`. Its
   guidance allows up to 50 unique input names, each at most 64 characters.
   The listed input `key` is the lower-cased name.
2. In Call a subflow, select the same object, active destination and record. Map
   `named_inputs.<input key>`. Missing named values arrive as empty text.
3. Resolve text identities to typed values inside the subflow when needed. The
   walkthrough passes an email and calls **Find workspace member**. Convert value
   cannot turn text into a workspace member.
4. Return using the current trigger's `subflow_id`, status and text outputs.
   The installed form saves an `outputs` array of objects containing `value`;
   UI says values follow the output order on Start a subflow. A waited successful return was verified in both caller and child logs;
   first-return-wins behavior remains documentation-backed.
5. The caller UI has **Wait for a result** (`wait_for_result`) and timeouts
   of 1, 3, 5, 10 or 15 minutes (`timeout_minutes`, string enum). The schema also
   retains optional legacy `dont_wait`. The one-minute no-Return case failed with an explicit timeout error after the child completed. Caller wall time was about 112 seconds; exact timer precision and other timeout choices remain unverified. A timeout does not roll back child effects.

Renaming inputs requires checking callers. Both caller and child run history
matter when debugging/retrying. The live installed controls supersede the older
fixed-15-minute/five-slot configuration descriptions for this bundle. The
second pass verified a complete waited caller/child roundtrip: named input
`identity_text` arrived, Return resolved this run's `subflow_id`, and the caller
received literal `result_text`. Pass 3 also verified two named inputs dynamically mapped to two returned outputs. A failed Return produced Call outcome `returned` with status `Failed` and a completed caller: inspect the status field, not just the run or branch. Non-waiting Call produced `started`, no returned fields, and an independently correlated child run. See pass-3 subflows for the timeout result and remaining limits.

Call stores `workflow_id` as a JSON-array string with **three** elements: callee
workflow UUID, Start trigger UUID, and an opaque token. Capture the complete UI
selection. A two-part value failed. In the 2026-10-22 picker probe, the token
was the same for two different callees in one workspace, so it isn't per
subflow, but it differed between workspaces. Its derivation is still unknown, but in i-5 (2026-10-22) it changed when the callee's outputs changed, and a People callee and a Companies callee had different tokens. It is likely derived from the output definitions, not from the subflow id. Re-pick after any output change.

## Scheduled runs: separate queue and execution evidence

Choose an object on Start a scheduled run and activate the destination. Schedule
matching records from the bulk **Schedule in workflow** action or from
**Schedule a workflow run**, which accepts the object, workflow, record and
future timestamp. The video composes native Adjust time with the scheduling step.

The bulk dialog uses organization time zone and quarter-hour choices. In the
live timestamp-step test, requested 18:32Z became scheduled_for 18:45Z. This
establishes normalization for that case, not a complete rounding algorithm.
Documentation says DST gaps are rejected and ambiguous repeated times use the
first occurrence; those cases were not runtime-tested. Separate scheduling actions
can create separate follow-ups. Pending schedules follow the workflow rather
than freezing its current version.

Turning a workflow off does not cancel its schedules; due runs may be skipped.
Deleting the record does not cancel them either. Check Upcoming/History and the
record widget. Portal cancellation supports individual/batch work, but a send
already underway cannot be cancelled. Reconcile partial batches before retrying.
**Sent means dispatch was accepted, not that downstream effects succeeded.**
Check the corresponding Attio run and block logs.

The [scheduling video at 07:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Kj6PLzf_Pg&t=421)
also narrates finding pending schedules and cancelling a selected next-run ID.
Both blocks were subsequently inspected in Playground:

- **Find scheduled runs** (`j-scheduled-runs-find`) has Object, Record,
  All workflows/Specific workflow, and Next run/All pending runs. Saved `all`
  selections use `workflow_scope` and `selection`.
- **Cancel scheduled runs** (`j-scheduled-runs-cancel`) offers a specific run ID
  or all pending runs for a record. The latter saves `mode=record` plus object.

The second pass created schedules, found exact pending IDs, cancelled one
specific ID and verified an empty queue. Specific cancellation saves `mode=run`.
Schedule selects a JSON-array string `[workflow UUID, Start trigger UUID]`; Find
with specific workflow instead saves the **raw workflow UUID**. Reusing one
selector shape in the other block failed. All/All and Specific/All Find modes
returned the expected single pending run. Pass 3 added two-item temporal ordering, Next-only selection, record-mode cancellation and repeated zero counters. The first due run completed through the corrected `scheduled` path into Convert; the remaining schedule was cancelled and Find returned zero. Connect to `scheduled`, not the earlier fixture’s mistaken `done` path. The trigger omits the queue ID, so queue-to-run attribution is correlated by exact owned Person, destination, due time and scheduled-by actor. Cancellation races remain untested. See pass-3 scheduling.

## Trigger and data edge cases

- Playground runtime verified all five task triggers, including completed and uncompleted branches, plus all three note triggers and Record deleted. The fresh fixtures were created before updates/deletion; this does not validate backfilled state or exhaustive event delivery. These app triggers have empty config and subscribe across the workspace.
- Task changes compare stored state. Initialize existing tasks through setup;
  first observation of an unknown task can establish a baseline without firing.
  Deleted-task deadline/completion fields may reflect creation/setup state;
  deadline outputs are date-only even when full timestamps were compared.
- Note title updated reacts to `note.updated` without comparing old/new titles.
  Note content updated supplies current text, not a previous body. Deleted notes
  cannot be fetched for title/body after deletion.
- The Playground data pass verified Find workspace member by ID returns a typed actor; Get comment returns its typed parent; Get thread returns first/last comment fields and count (no parent field in the installed output). Pass 3 verified an ordered two-comment thread, reply getter, and missing comment/thread results. Email member lookup/normalization and case-sensitive absence were also tested.
- **Move note copies then attempts deletion.** A synthetic move was independently verified: distinct new note ID on target B, title/plaintext preserved, source GET404. Further public readbacks verified Markdown and meeting-link preservation; the temporary meeting-linked note was removed after testing. It creates a new ID/author/time;
  comments and attachments do not migrate. A deletion failure can leave both
  notes even when the step succeeds. Rerunning Create note can also duplicate.
- Runtime Find tasks with an exact open task ID returned count1 for completion Any and count0 for is_complete, both with has_more_matches=false. An exact ID does not bypass filters. Pass 3 added all deadline-status choices, exact before/after boundaries, linked-record match, assignee mismatch, and invalid completion/deadline combinations.
- App Find tasks has flat documented options, **not native Find Records filter
  grammar**. Set completion explicitly: current UI defaults to Any, but a missing
  saved value means open. Overdue filters force open tasks. Before is exclusive,
  after inclusive. Task/note scans may be incomplete: check `has_more_matches`.
- Runtime negative cases differ: Get meeting with empty ID completed with `found=false`; Get call transcript with both IDs empty failed with `Choose Meeting ID and Call recording ID.` A populated read-only meeting was subsequently verified against public metadata without retaining its text/participant identities. A bounded recording scan found no fixture; the token lacks recording-write scope. Valid transcript content and recording-created delivery remain untested.
- Get call transcript needs both meeting and recording IDs; it does not poll.
  Handle `not_ready` with bounded retry logic and `has_more_matches` as incomplete.
  Get thread returns first/last bodies, not every comment. Get meeting does not
  return participant attendance status.
- Actual Compare records A,A → B,A returned added=1, removed=0, changed=1, unchanged=1; Compare members [] → self,self returned one added/changed member. Pass 3 adds removal, empty sets and order-only cases plus domain/phone inputs. Outcome `changed` can still have changed.count=0; inspect counts.
- Compare ignores order/duplicates. `added` means new-only, `removed` previous-only,
  `changed` symmetric difference, `unchanged` intersection. Check primary value is
  documented but was absent from the inspected Playground picker. Swapping A/B changes added/removed even though the
  symmetric difference stays the same.

## Diagnose using both products

Platform Activity reports app events, not all blocks in an Attio workflow.
Acknowledging an item records review; it does not fix or rerun it. Scheduled runs
tracks dispatch/subflow activity. Attio run and block logs show complete workflow
execution. A retryable app error flag is not proof that a retry happened.

Use Count 0, Found false, `invalid_input`, `not_ready`, and empty outcomes as
explicit paths. Review already completed effects before retrying. Documented machine
keys/types remain in the original dated catalog. Consult the live catalog for
installed schemas and saved config first where available; neither alone proves
execution. The first Create folder probe omitted required `object` and failed
conversion. Supplying it produced `created` and `was_created=true`. Pass 3 returned the same ID with `was_created=false` on reuse; the read-only Files UI and record-scoped storage endpoint independently verified exact ID/name. Public Files readback remained forbidden.

Get primary value currently emits `completed` and a text `primary`, including empty text for an explicitly empty array; omitted Values fails validation. This differs from documented Found/Empty branches. Email, domain and phone arrays were tested. Convert value keeps typed-string outputs even for number/boolean targets; date validation, offset-to-UTC conversion and empty input cases are in pass-3 data evidence. HTML script/style removal is verified only for the exact captured fixture, not a general security guarantee.

The guarded latest-run helper now reads workflow-level `/runs/latest`, validates workspace/workflow ownership and rejects a latest run belonging to a different requested immutable version. It is not per-version history. See the pass-3 regression and remote-read evidence.
